headline: Butuan Airport Operations Suspended After Aircraft Blocks Runway
deck: A disabled aircraft on the runway temporarily stopped takeoffs and landings at Butuan Airport and led to 11 flight cancellations on August 9.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The Civil Aviation Authority of the Philippines temporarily suspended landing and takeoff operations at Butuan Airport on Sunday, August 9, after a disabled aircraft blocked the runway.

sections.heading: What we know
paragraphs: CAAP listed 11 canceled departures. Cebu Pacific canceled Butuan-Manila flights 5J 786, 5J 794, 5J 792, 5J 788 and 5J 790. Cebgo canceled Butuan-Cebu flights DG 6930, DG 6926 and DG 6924.
Philippine Airlines canceled Butuan-Cebu flight PR 2334 and Butuan-Manila flights PR 2942 and PR 2939.
CAAP said the affected airlines offered passengers available rebooking, refund or travel-fund options.

sections.heading: Background
paragraphs: Butuan Airport, also known as Bancasi Airport, is a key aviation gateway for Butuan City and the wider Caraga region. A runway obstruction prevents normal aircraft movements until the operating area can be cleared and declared safe.

sections.heading: What remains unclear
paragraphs: The CAAP advisory did not identify the disabled aircraft, state what caused it to become immobilized or provide a definite time for normal operations to resume.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: The suspension affected travel between Caraga, Manila and Cebu. Clear flight information is important for passengers deciding whether to proceed to the airport or arrange a refund or replacement journey.

sections.heading: What happens next
paragraphs: Passengers should verify their latest flight status directly with their airline before going to the airport. CAAP said it would continue monitoring airport operations in coordination with government agencies and airline operators.
